item.title: India Rupee roars back on RBI’s support, up most in seven months
item.description: India’s central bank stepped in forcefully to support the rupee, propelling it to the biggest gain in seven months in a move that some analysts said was intended to punish those betting on a one-way slide in the currency. The rupee rose as much as 1%, the most since May 23, to 90.0963 on Wednesday, after closing at a record low in the previous session. item.title: Over 100 flights cancelled at Delhi airport as city wakes up to thick fog
item.description: More than 100 flights were cancelled at Delhi’s airport on Saturday as dense fog reduced visibility across the North India and disrupted air traffic. Officials said at least 66 arriving flights and 63 departures were cancelled at the at the Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport amid the weather conditions. item.title: Montclair, New Jersey: NJ Transit train derailment leaves 17 injured; first details out
item.description: At least 17 people were injured in a NJ Transit train derailment in Montclair, New Jersey, on Friday, December 19. The incident took place just after 6:45 pm. It remains unclear if only one train derailed or both. Service along the Montclair Boonton Line was halted for hours on Friday after two trains made contact, causing a minor derailment. item.title: Jammu & Kashmir To Host First International Indian Style Wrestling Event Today
item.description: Jammu and Kashmir is all set to host its first-ever International Indian Style Wrestling (Dangal) event along with Rustam-e-Jammu Kashmir Title 2025 at the iconic Maulana Azad Stadium, Jammu, today. The mega sporting event will witness participation of more than 100 International and National Dangal stars who will compete for the Rustam-e-Jammu Kashmir Title 2025. The competition will also feature open-category bouts with prominent national and international wrestlers.

item.title: Dense fog covered Delhi as the AQI hit 384, pushing air quality to the edge of the ‘severe’ zone.
item.description: Dense fog hit Delhi, cutting visibility and pushing AQI to 384, near ‘severe’, causing major travel disruptions. Delhi reeled under severe weather and pollution conditions on Saturday as dense fog blanketed large parts of the national capital, drastically reducing visibility and pushing air quality to dangerous levels. Thick, toxic smog has engulfed Delhi as air quality plunged into the ‘severe’ zone. With AQI hitting 420 near Akshardham, CAQM has enforced GRAP Stage-IV measures across Delhi-NCR
